newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker and Super League executive director Ian Frykberg have held another day of merger talks. Balmain club chief executive Danny Munk says five ARL clubs have indicated they are willing to discuss mergers. Page 20.

Super League has admitted that Cronulla should have been awarded two tries in their match against Auckland last week, while there is significant doubt about Auckland's only try. A video error meant that the only angle of a possible Cronulla try that would have proven its legality was not available at the time. Game referee Phil Houston has been sacked after two controversial performances and reduced to reserve grade. Page 20.

Six changes have been made to the Australian rugby union side after last week's loss to New Zealand. The team plays England this weekend, with former Test captain Phil Kearns again overlooked for the team after returning from injury recently. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Oil industry executive Ric Charlton was yesterday appointed the new National Basketball League chairman, replacing Mal Speed who is now the chief executive of the Australian Cricket Board. Charlton believes his challenge will be to address a recent drop-off in support for the competition. Page 47.

Australian cricketer Shane Warne has attracted controversy in the British newspaper tabloids after giving Manchester fans a "one-finger" salute following Australia's victory in the Third Test. Warne denied making the gesture, but photographs of various Warne antics have made a number of local papers. Page 48. --

Australian cyclists are performing well in the Tour de France, with Stuart O'Grady leading the field at one stage yesterday. Australia has five riders in the race, where both stages have been won so far by Mario Cipollini. Page 46.
THE AGE

The North Melbourne Australian Football League club has requested that the AFL investigate an incident that left North's Sam McFarlane with a broken jaw. McFarlane will not play for the remainder of the season, with St Kilda forward Barry Hill under question over the incident. Page B16.

The Australian under-20 women's basketball team has won their latest match at the world junior championships, defeating Spain by 53-41. Coach Ray Tomlinson has criticised the design of the basketball stadium, claiming a wind is blown across the court and had cost the team an opening round win. Page B14.

Leading Australian golfer Greg Norman says he felt concerned for his safety at recent tournaments, and has called for increased protection in upcoming events. Norman says an alcohol ban after mid-afternoon at tournaments could ease the problem. Page B16.
THE HERALD SUN

The decision over the future of Australian Football League club Hawthorn's coach Ken Judge could be determined tonight at a board meeting when discussions between Judge and his management are announced. The club is likely to offer Judge a further two years on his contract, with Judge being sought by rival clubs Carlton and West Coast. Page 80.

Three touring car drivers are in a battle for the championship, with Glenn Seton, Russell Ingall and John Bowe all capable of winning. All three failed to score points in last week's round, and only two rounds are remaining for the title. Page 71.

North Melbourne Australian Football League player Anthony Stevens may wear a protective helmet in this week's game against Geelong after recent knocks to the head. Stevens has no serious medical concerns, and would wear the helmet as a protective measure Page 78.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Troubled Australian Rugby League player Julian O'Neill has returned to first grade at the South Sydney club this weekend after being dropped from last week's game after missing a training session. Souths coach Ken Shine says there was no pressure from tem-mates to keep O'Neill out of the team, saying that inmates don't run the jail. Page 77.

Australian basketball player Michelle Timms scored 11 points for the Phoenix Mercury as they defeated the New York Liberty 69-50 in the latest round of the Women's National Basketball Association. Liberty player Rebecca Lobo suffered her first defeat in 102 games. Page 70.

The Australian junior men's water polo team have won the last game and the series at a three-nation tournament in Slovakia yesterday. The competition against Slovakia and Slovenia is good preparation for the world junior championships, starting on July 1. Page 70.
